title: Heterogeneous prefill gating and admission control for tail-latency smoothing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As our continuous batching surface supports more mixed workloads (short chat turns, long completions, embedding prefill requests, and multi-tenant variance), we see an increased number of outlier tail latencies caused by large heterogeneous batches that force kernel choices and KV cache behavior suboptimally. Current admission only considers queue length and simple token budgets which leads to (1) individual requests waiting for oversized prefills, (2) kernels being chosen for worst-case sequences, and (3) per-tenant SLO violations during traffic spikes.

Goal: Implement a prefill gating and admission-control layer that is aware of heterogeneous batch composition and per-tenant tail risk. The new system should: 1) preferentially admit requests that preserve efficient kernel matches, 2) limit cross-tenant head-of-line blocking by per-tenant slot reservations, and 3) introduce a lightweight per-request latency risk score to guide admission and trigger fast-path decode allocation.

Proposed approach:
- Introduce a compact PrefillDescriptor attached to each prefill request (length, streaming hint, quantization-class, tenant-id, kernel-preference score). This descriptor is evaluated by the admission controller (no full model introspection).
- Maintain an adaptive bucket histogram of in-flight prefill shapes (short/medium/long) per-GPU and per-queue; admission favors maintaining a target composition that keeps kernels in their sweet spot.
- Compute a per-request LatencyRisk = f(remaining_prefill_tokens, tenant_tail_exposure, is_streamed). LatencyRisk above threshold routes the request to the fast-path queue which preallocates smaller decode slots with strict KV cache warm-start.
- Per-tenant soft reservations: lightweight tokens that guarantee a minimal admission throughput for tenants with tight SLOs, reclaimed on idle.
- Kernel-match scoring: when forming a candidate batch, score kernel compatibility weighted by expected sequence length and quantization class; if score below fallback, trigger admission splitting instead of forcing a kernel mismatch.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Extra CPU overhead in the admission path to compute histograms and scores; we will optimize by using lock-free ring buffers and approximate counters.
- PrefillDescriptor leaks minimal metadata; privacy review required for tenant-id usage in scheduler (we only use opaque tenant hash).
- Risk of increased small batches hurting throughput; mitigate by dynamic thresholds that relax during low-concurrency windows.

Success metrics: reduce 99.9p latency for multi-tenant small-requests-by-large-prefill scenario by 35% while keeping overall throughput degradation <5%.

Notes on compatibility: integrates with existing kernel-selection API (kernel registry) and the KV cache warm-start hooks. Backwards compatible: if PrefillDescriptor is missing, admission falls back to current behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Deployable admission controller with PrefillDescriptor support behind a feature flag
99.9p tail latency improvement >= 30% for mixed short/long request workload in benchmark cluster
Throughput drop <= 5% in steady-state synthetic load
Per-tenant reservation honors configured guarantees and is reclaimable
Unit and integration tests for latency risk scoring and kernel-match fallback
